findings.title: Elecbrakes EB2, VM1, ELBC2000 (ICS advisory ICSA-26-323-02)
findings.summary_md: CISA published ICS advisory ICSA-26-323-02 on 19 November 2026 for Elecbrakes EB2 through version 3.0.4.2.0, VM1 below 1.3.4.2.1 and all ELBC2000 controllers. It lists CVE-2026-96805 and CVE-2026-125273 at CVSS 3.1 9.6 for missing authentication and replayable BLE commands, plus CVE-2026-124281 at 6.1 for an unprotected firmware-update channel. The advisory says exploitation could let an attacker control trailer brakes, modify firmware, disable brake lights or other safety features, and that no public exploitation had been reported to CISA at release.

findings.title: Brake Check: Hijacking Trailer Brakes Over Bluetooth (Element Digital)
findings.summary_md: Patrick Forck and Jeremy McCarthy of Element Digital published a technical write-up on 19 November 2026 describing four-byte unauthenticated writes to an Elecbrakes brake-control BLE characteristic, with no pairing, PIN or replay protection and notification feedback on brake state. They report testing on their own hardware, including a closed-road drive test where higher force values produced stronger deceleration, and an OTA channel reachable after Just Works pairing with firmware integrity checked only by CRC32. The post says the vendor shipped fixes on 6 July 2026 for EB2 3.0.4.4.3 and VM1 1.3.4.2.1, left the older ELBC 2000 without a fix, and found no evidence of exploitation.

findings.title: Critical Bluetooth Flaws in Elecbrakes Trailer Controllers Allow Remote Brake Hijacking (Hispion)
findings.summary_md: Hispion reported on 19 November 2026 that nearby attackers could manipulate braking, flash modified firmware and disable brake lights over BLE without pairing on Elecbrakes EB2, VM1 and ELBC2000 controllers. The article names CVE-2026-96805, CVE-2026-125273 and CVE-2026-124281, with maximum CVSS 3.1 score 9.6, and notes that fixes exist for EB2 and VM1 but not the discontinued ELBC2000. It says authorities confirmed no evidence of active in-the-wild exploitation at disclosure and places the devices in Australia and New Zealand transportation.

findings.title: CISA ICS Advisories Warn of Elecbrakes, OpenPLC, and libumqtt Flaws (Meterpreter)
findings.summary_md: Meterpreter's 20 November 2026 roundup covered CISA's 19 November ICS advisories and placed the Elecbrakes BLE brake bugs beside OpenPLC Runtime and libumqtt flaws. It reports CVE-2026-96805 and CVE-2026-125273 at 9.6 for missing authentication and replay, and CVE-2026-124281 at 6.1 for firmware updates, quoting CISA's warning about brake control, firmware modification and disabled brake lights. The article says no known public attacks or live exploits were known at publication.

findings.title: CISA said Elecbrakes trailer brake controller flaws could let attackers control the brakes (SDV Sector)
findings.summary_md: SDV Sector reported on 20 November 2026 that three CISA-listed flaws in Elecbrakes EB2, VM1 and ELBC2000 controllers could let attackers control trailer brakes, change firmware or disable brake lights. It says fixes reach owners only if they install them through the Elecbrakes app, and that the discontinued ELBC2000 has no fix. CISA told the outlet that no known public exploitation of the flaws had been reported.

findings.title: Hackers can slam on Bluetooth-connected trailer brakes, researchers find (iTnews)
findings.summary_md: iTnews reported on 20 November 2026 that any Bluetooth device within 10 to 100 metres could apply full brakes on un-updated Elecbrakes EB2, VM1 and ELBC 2000 controllers, with a jackknife or loss of control as the stated risk. It names researchers Patrick Forck and Jeremy McCarthy and cites CVE-2026-96805 and CVE-2026-125273 at CVSS 9.6 and CVE-2026-124281 at 6.1. The article says Elecbrakes told it 60 to 70 percent of connecting controllers were then running the latest firmware, while the discontinued ELBC range still awaited remediation.
